findings.title: Reintroduction of SSRF/Local File Read via SpatialReference (CVE-2026-114582)
findings.description:
This diff reverts the security fix for CVE-2026-114582. The changes remove all protections that prevented GDAL from resolving URLs and reading local files when parsing user-supplied spatial reference strings:

1. **Removal of `PAPSZ_OPTIONS`** (ALLOW_FILE_ACCESS=NO, ALLOW_NETWORK_ACCESS=NO): Without these options, GDAL's `OSRSetFromUserInput` will freely resolve URLs (SSRF) and read local files when a user-controlled string is passed to `SpatialReference()`.

2. **Removal of `OSRSetFromUserInputEx` call**: The code now unconditionally uses `OSRSetFromUserInput` (which has no options parameter) instead of `OSRSetFromUserInputEx` (which accepts the blocking options on GDAL ≥ 3.9).

3. **Removal of DICT: prefix rejection**: The dictionary parser bypass in GDAL (which ignores file access restrictions) is no longer blocked. An attacker can use `DICT:` or `ESRI::DICT:` prefixed strings to read arbitrary files regardless of GDAL version.

4. **Removal of `gis.W001` security check**: Operators will no longer be warned when running a vulnerable GDAL version.

5. **Removal of all regression tests**: The tests that verified file access blocking, network access blocking, and dictionary rejection are deleted.

**Attack vector**: Any application that passes user-controlled input to `SpatialReference(string)`, `GEOSGeometry.transform(srs=string)`, `OGRGeometry.transform(srs=string)`, `GDALRaster.transform(srs=string)`, or the `.srs`/`.srid` setters is vulnerable. An attacker supplying `https://attacker.com/evil` triggers an outbound SSRF request; supplying `/etc/passwd` or a `.prj` file path reads local files; supplying `DICT:/path/to/file,4326` bypasses all GDAL file-access restrictions on any version.
findings.suggestion:
Restore the security mitigations that were removed:

```python
from django.contrib.gis.gdal.error import GDALException, SRSException
from django.contrib.gis.gdal.libgdal import GDAL_VERSION
from ctypes import c_char_p, byref

# Create null terminated gdal options array.
papsz_options = [
    b"ALLOW_FILE_ACCESS=NO",
    b"ALLOW_NETWORK_ACCESS=NO",
    None,
]
PAPSZ_OPTIONS = (c_char_p * len(papsz_options))(*papsz_options)

def import_user_input(self, user_input):
    "Import the Spatial Reference from the given user input string."
    user_input = force_bytes(user_input)
    # GDAL's dictionary parser bypasses its file access restrictions.
    if user_input.lstrip().lower().removeprefix(b"esri::").startswith(b"dict:"):
        msg = "Spatial references from dictionaries are not supported."
        raise GDALException(msg)
    if GDAL_VERSION < (3, 9):
        capi.from_user_input(self.ptr, user_input)
    else:
        capi.from_user_input_ex(self.ptr, user_input, byref(PAPSZ_OPTIONS))
```

Also restore `checks.py`, the `gis.W001` check registration, and the regression tests. If this reversion is intentional (e.g., the CVE was false-positive), the release notes and documentation should explicitly explain why the SSRF risk is now accepted and what compensating controls operators must apply.

findings.title: Removal of security system check (gis.W001) eliminates operator visibility into vulnerable GDAL versions
findings.description: The `check_gdal_39` check and its `gis` tag are deleted from `django/contrib/gis/apps.py`, `django/contrib/gis/checks.py`, and `django/core/checks/registry.py`. This check warned operators when their installed GDAL version (< 3.9) could not enforce file/network access restrictions. Without this check, operators running GDAL < 3.9 have no indication they are exposed to SSRF via `SpatialReference` string inputs.
findings.suggestion: If the SSRF mitigation is being intentionally reverted, retain the `gis.W001` check (or an equivalent) so operators are still informed when their GDAL version lacks native access-restriction support. Alternatively, document a clear upgrade requirement in the installation guide.

findings.title: Deletion of regression tests for SSRF/file-read protections
findings.description: All tests validating the security behavior (`test_no_dictionary_access`, `test_no_file_access`, `test_no_network_access`, `test_esri_prefixed_wkt`) are removed from `tests/gis_tests/gdal_tests/test_srs.py`, and `tests/gis_tests/test_checks.py` is deleted entirely. This removes the safety net that would catch future regressions of the SSRF fix.
findings.suggestion: If the protections are restored (see CRITICAL finding), restore these tests. If the revert is intentional, add tests that document the now-accepted behavior and any compensating input validation that applications must perform.
